Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all we have from this match. We look forward to your company for future games. Until we meet again, it's goodbye and cheers.

VICTORIOUS SOUTH AFRICAN SKIPPER, FAF DU PLESSIS says that he was unsure at the toss and would have probably bowled. Adds that each batsman scoring a fifty set the tone for them initially. Accepts the conditions weren't suitable to bat freely but their batting unit put the hands up and accepted the challenge. About his knock, he is absolutely delighted and also says captaining the side has its own sweet taste. On his bowlers, he says they kept creating the pressure and feels they made the task easy for the team. Ends by saying, the next series against Australia will be a tough one but the result of this Test has given them a positive attitude.

MAN OF THE MATCH, QUINTON DE KOCK is very happy to open the innings and playing a positive role in this match. Thinks he rode his luck and at the same time had a set mind to go out and play aggressive cricket. Furthers says, he doesn't mind batting down the order and is more keen to do what his team wants from him. Accepts it wasn't easy to keep behind the wickets on a pitch like this and feels he can totally understand BJ Watling's condition at the moment.

NEW ZEALAND SKIPPER, KANE WILLIAMSON says his finger is alright now. Further says, the pitch was not an easy one to bat on. Credits South Africa for outclassing him and his team. Is happy that his side still showed some fight after getting rocked early. Emphasizes on the fact that the four South African players scored fifties and their bowlers did all the damage. Praises Henry Nicholls for the way he played today. On the upcoming series, he replies they will go home for a week and then will head to India.

The "Steyn Gun" fired and ran through the Kiwi top half in a jiffy. The lower middle order did offer some resistance but it wasn't enough as South Africa eventually went on to register their second biggest win over New Zealand in terms of runs.

Second time around, the Kiwi bowlers got a lot of purchase from the pitch and were tough to handle. They had the Protea batsmen on their knees but the lead that they had conceded proved fatal. South Africa eventually set a target of 400 this morning and then their bowlers wreaked havoc.

New Zealand might be regretting their decision to bowl first. Their bowling wasn't up to the mark as South Africa managed to post a mammoth first innings total. Unlike the Kiwis, the South African bowlers were right on the money and managed to gain a massive lead.

Magnificent victory for South Africa as they take the series 1-0! Dale Steyn was the real star and proved to the world that he is not done yet. He finished with 8 wickets in this Test match and bowled with a lot of fire and venom.

OUT! It's all over for New Zealand! Steyn picks up his 26th 5-wicket haul in Tests and is all pumped up. A superb display of all round cricket from the Proteas. Short of a length delivery down leg, Nicholls looks to pull but only manages to get a top edge which is easily grabbed by Rabada at long leg. A good fighting knock from Nicholls comes to an end. SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 204 RUNS!
Short of a length delivery on middle, Nicholls defends it off the back foot.
DALE STEYN is back on.
TRENT BOULT is the last batsman.

OUT! This was on the cards after the bombardment of short balls to Wagner. Rabada sets him nicely for a yorker, around middle, Wagner is stuck inside the crease and then tries to dig it out. But he is beaten for sheer pace and is hit on the back pad. They appeal and the finger is up immediately. One more wicket left for a 1-0 series win.
Rabada ups his pace and bullets a length ball wide outside off, 145.4 kph, Wagner swishes and misses.
Sharp length ball on off, Wagner tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Here comes the bouncer. Good pace but the line is too easy for the batsman to evade. He needs to target those near Wagner's rib-cage.
The square leg fielder moves on the off side. A leg slip, short leg, deep square leg in place too. More short stuff coming...
Good length ball on off, Wagner goes back and hits it through covers for a couple of runs.
Bouncer down the leg side, it's left alone by Wagner. Wayward bowling this by him. It's a tail-ender in front of him and he should be looking to fire in yorkers.

Good delivery but nicely played as well. On a length and in the line of the stumps, a hint of away movement, Wagner brings down a straight bat and pushes it through mid off for a single. Retains strike. Hmm...
Slips a full length ball down the leg side, the batsman fails to flick it.
Bouncer around off, Wagner shows respect and bows down to let it go over his head.
Play and a miss! Full in length and outside off, holding its line, Wagner plays inside the line and gets beaten. Nearly edged it.
Angles across a length ball outside off, Wagner pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Lands it on a fuller length around off, Wagner defends it off his front foot.
VERNON PHILANDER is back on!

FOUR! Bang! Width on offer outside off, Nicholls has batted for so long that he is now used to the pace and bounce of this pitch. He latches onto this one and smacks it through the gap between gully and point for a boundary.

Shout for an lbw! Not given. Rabada goes for a rip-roaring yorker, around leg, Wagner fails to get bat on ball and is hit on the pads. They put in an unsuccessful appeal as the batsmen cross over for a leg bye. Faf du Plessis looks at his bowler but Kagiso is not confident enough. Hence no DRS taken. The replays confirm that it would have missed leg.
A length delivery down the leg side, Wagner tries flicking but fails to connect.
NEIL WAGNER is in next.

OUT! Rabada gets his revenge! He dishes out a brilliant yorker, right at the base of the off stump, it's too quick for Southee to dig out and the stumps take a beating. The umpire quickly checks for the front foot no ball and it's found out to be a legal delivery in the replays. Rabada has the last laugh in this contest. South Africa only two wickets away from winning the series.
FOUR! Boom! This one is in the slot for Tim, around off and on a fuller length, he gets forward and thwacks it over covers for a boundary.
EDGED AND FOUR! Quickfire delivery, short and wide outside off, Southee has a wild hoick at it and the outside edge flies over the jumping first slip fielder for a boundary.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
It's on a driving length around off, Nicholls could have driven it but reads the away movement before leaving it untouched.
This one is very wide outside off, Nicholls has nothing to do with it.
Angles across a length ball outside off, left alone with ease by Nicholls.
Great ball, full around off, shaping in a touch, Nicholls tries to defend from the crease but it comes off the inside edge and rolls towards mid-wicket.
Full in length around leg, Nicholls gets behind the line and defends it back to the bowler.
Rabada fires in a full ball on off, Southee this time connects with his blind heave and it goes over extra cover. The ball falls safely and they take a couple of runs.
Southee is trying his best to get out but is not successful. Short delivery this time, Tim tries his best to play an upper cut but fails to connect. It nearly took the outside edge.
Good length ball landing outside off and shaping back in, Southee stays back and punches it to covers.
Sharp delivery, a touch short and on off, Southee winds up for another big shot but once again fails to make any connection.
Play and a miss! Full in length and wide outside off, Southee throws his bat at it but fails to make any connection.
Back of a length ball on middle, Nicholls helps it off the inside half of the bat to mid-wicket and crosses for a single.
FOUR! Fuller length ball on off, Southee makes room and lofts it past mid off for a boundary.

A LOUD SHOUT FOR CAUGHT BEHIND! On a length and wide outside off, Southee swings his bat and it goes back to the keeper. They all go up in appeal and the umpire stays unmoved. Replays show there was no wood involved there.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball but fails.
On a length and outside off, Southee goes after it only to miss.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Good length ball on off, Southee looks to play at it but gets beaten.
FOUR LEG BYES! Short of a length delivery on middle, Nicholls ducks to evade it but the ball hits him on his arms and goes over the slip cordon for a boundary.
HN defends it from within the crease.
In the channel outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms to that one.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Fuller length delivery on middle, flicked towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! Slashed! Short of a length delivery on off, gives a bit of width too. It is enough for Nicholls to cut it behind point for a boundary.
KAGISO RABADA is brought back!
Fuller length ball on off, defended off the front foot.
TIM SOUTHEE is the new man in!

OUT! The decision stays as it is! Philander strikes and that's the end of Bracewell! Vernon hurls a length delivery on middle, skids off the deck after pitching. Doug looks to flick it across the line but misses only to be rapped on the pads. Philander appeals and it's given out straightaway. The batsman isn't convinced with the decision and hence takes the review. The replays show it was pitched in line and was clipping the leg stump. Umpire's call and Bracewell's cameo comes to an end.
Dough Bracewell is given out LBW. He has opted to go for the review.
Beaten up! Fuller length delivery on off, moving away a bit. Bracewell looks to go after it but is beaten.
Shortish on off, Dough defends it with a straight bat.
FOUR! Uppish but safe! Fuller length delivery on off, Bracewell lofts it magnificently over covers. Clears the infield and fetches himself a boundary. The stand is worth 46 off 46 balls.
Good length ball on middle, DB defends it from within the crease.
VERNON PHILANDER is brought back into the attack!
Tossed up around middle and off, Nicholls defends it down.
Flattish on middle, tucked past short leg for a single.
Full and around middle, Bracewell defends it down.

SIX! Down the track and away she goes! Loopy ball around middle and off, Bracewell gets down the track and hits it hard over the bowler's head for a maximum all the way. Bracewell is taking his chances.
Loopy ball around off, Bracewell lunges forward and drives it straight to covers.
Tossed up around off, driven towards mid off for a single.
Drinks break...
On a length and outside off, DB gets back and taps it on the off side.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Angles a length delivery on middle, Bracewell looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. An appeal is made but that can't be given as it was missing leg clearly.
FOUR! Sweetly timed! Fuller length delivery on off, Doug leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary.
On a length and outside off, Bracwell looks to poke at it but gets beaten up.
Fuller length delivery on off, blocked back to the bowler.
FOUR! Swept away beautifully! Beautifully tossed up around middle and leg, Henry gets down on one knee and sweeps it elegantly through backward square leg. One bounce and into the ropes she goes.
Short and outside off, Nicholls eyes to hit it through point but is lucky as the ball falls just short of the man at backward point.
Flattish on middle, Nicholls gets back and flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Full and around middle, driven past the man at mid on for a single.
Tossed up around off, turns in after pitching. Bracewell covers the line and defends it down.
Short and around off, Nicholls gets back and cuts it through point for a single.
Well outside off, Bracewell shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! PUNCHED! Bracewell faces down Steyn and comes out on top! This is a shortish delivery and Bracewell hangs back to punch it uppishly through point for a boundary.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Bracewell chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Fuller ball outside off, Bracewell leaves it.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
FOUR! TASTEFULLY DONE! Short and outside off, Nicholls leans across and swipes at it. That was some solid contact and the ball rockets through point for a boundary.
Served on the pads, flicked to the leg side for a single.

SIX! EXCELLENTLY DONE! It is Bracewell's turn to come down the track. Landed outside off, he steps forward to the pitch of the ball and lofts it straight down the ground and into the air. That was very well struck and deceptive in its power. It hangs in the air and lands well into the stands for a massive maximum.
Floated on middle and leg, worked down the leg side.
Flighted on the stumps, worked to mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! POSITIVE STROKE! Nicholls shows great sense of the pitch here. Full ball outside off, Nicholls makes good use of his feet, sliding forward to loft that one up simply. It flies over mid off and across the boundary line.
Back of a length delivery around off, defended from within the crease.
Good length ball on middle and off, pushed through mid on for a couple.
Shortish ball on middle and off, it's a clever delivery and Bracewell does well to defend it.
Length ball outside off, Bracewell plays it to point.
Short delivery, Bracewell blocks it off the back foot with the full face of his bat.
Down the leg side, Bracewell tries to flick it but misses.
Shorter ball outside off, punched off the back foot to the covers for a single.
Length ball outside off and swinging in sharply, Bracewell works it to mid-wicket.
Slower and fuller on off, Bracewell comes forward again and defends it.
Length ball outside off, blocked off the front foot.
Shortish delivery, Henry plays it to mid-wicket for a single.
Very full on the stumps, driven to the covers.
DOUG BRACEWELL comes to the wicket.

OUT! Knocked him over! The middle stump is out of here. Can imagine the pace of Dale Steyn. Dale has absolutely nailed it. He comes from round the wicket, bowls a full length ball angling in, at 137.7 kph. Santner without any foot movement looks to drive but is beaten for pace as the ball goes right through bat and pad to disturb the furniture. South Africa just need 4 wickets to win now. Note - Dale Steyn becomes the leading wickettaker in Centurion now, goes past Makhaya Ntini's 54.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Fuller length ball on off, Nicholls pushes it towards covers.
On a length and around off, Nicholls leaves it alone.
Angles a length ball on middle, Santenr gets an inside edge towards fine leg for a single.

FOUR! Edged and dropped! Santner survives the scare here and Amla is the culprit here. Steyn is not happy and starts to walk back. Short of a length delivery on off, moves away a bit. Santner looks to play it inside the line and ends up getting an outside edge towards first slip where Amla drops a simple catch. To add to that that, the ball parries off his palms and runs down to third man for a boundary. Amla seems to have hurt his finger. It's bleeding and he starts to sprint towards the dressing room.
Full and around middle, Henry defends it watchfully.
Loopy ball around middle and off, Nicholls defends it down.
Nicholls failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads.
Gets behind the line and defends it down.
Ahhh.. That was not a good leave to be honest. Tosses this one up around off, Nicholls leans forward and lets this on go through him. It goes very close to the off stick.
Floated ball around middle, pushed back to the bowler off the front foot.
Short of a length ball on off, at 140.4 kph, Santner leaves it for alone.
Short of a length delivery down the leg side, Mitchell ducks to let that one sail over him to the keeper.
Short of a length delivery on off, Henry stands tall and taps it on the off side.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Back of a length ball on off, defended with a straight bat.
2nd Test fifty for Henry Nicholls!
Good length ball on off, Nicholls gets behind and dabs it towards gully for a single. What an innings this has been. When others failed, he stepped up with a memorable knock.
Quicker and flatter again, on middle, hit across the line and it went off short leg to mid-wicket. Piedt ran to collect the ball.
Flatter ball on middle, it's punched back to the bowler.
Santner has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up ball outside off, left alone.
Floated ball on off, Santner gets forward and defends it watchfully.
Appeal for an lbw! A slider from round the wicket, landing on middle and skidding down, the batsman is cramped for room and is hit on the pads. They appeal but it's missing leg.
Nicholls is getting some treatment here. He has hurt his finger while facing that short ball in the previous over by Steyn. The physio is out and tapping his finger.
Banged short on middle, Nicholls ducks to evade it.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Short of a length delivery on off, Nicholls stands tall and defends it towards the off side.
Shortish on middle and leg, Santner tucks it towards square leg for a single.
That was a sharp bumper! Dale bangs it short on off, angling in a bit. Santner arches back and lets it go past him to de Kock.
Good length delivery on off, stays low as well. Santner looks to drive but the ball goes beneath his bat towards the keeper.
FOUR! Short and turns away after pitching. Henry gets back into the crease and slams it through point for a blazing boundary. Moves onto 49 now!
Full and around middle, Nicholls defends it from within the crease.
Drops it short and around off, Santner gets back and punches it towards covers for a single.
Short and outside off, Mitchell makes an easy leave.
Full and around off, defended off the front foot gently.
Tossed up around middle and off, punched off the back foot through cover-point for a single.
Angles a length delivery on the pads, tucked behind square on the leg side for a single.
In the channel outside off, HN lifts his bat and allows it to go through to the keeper.
On a length and around off, Santner opens the face of the bat and guides it towards point for one.
Steyn bangs it short on middle, Santner ducks to evade it.
Short of a length delivery on middle, pulled through mid-wicket for an easy single.
Back of a length ball outside off, Henry punches it off the back foot towards covers.
DALE STEYN is back on!
Full and around middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! That's slashed! Short and around off, Nicholls gets back and cuts it hard through cover-point for a boundary.
Flighted ball around off, Nicholls pushes it towards covers.

Bye! That's beaten! Tossed up around middle and off, Santner makes room to drive but the ball turns away and goes just past the off stick. de Kock and Amla both couldn't stop the ball and they take a bye.
Loopy ball around middle and off, turns away after pitching. Santner leaves it alone.
Tossed up around middle and off, Santner drives it straight to the man at mid off.

Welcome back for the final session, folks! Could be the last one of this series as well but that remains to be seen. For now we have both the Kiwi batsmen out. DANE PIEDT to begin the bowling proceedings. Let's play...
DAY 4, SESSION 3...

Overs - 28, Runs - 77, Wickets - 01. A session which has not gone the way most of us thought. New Zealand batted bravely and lost only one wicket in it. Watling and Nicholls adopted a watchful approach and were involved in a 68-run stand. However, Watling was removed later on by Dane Piedt. South Africa bowled well but were not as lethal as they were in the first session. With 5 more wickets left for a win, let's see for how long New Zealand can battle. Do join us in a short while...
Once again a very full ball around leg, Nicholls tries to flick but is beaten for pace. TEA ON DAY 4!
A cracking yorker, around leg and drifting down, Santner tries to dig it out but misses and it goes off his pads past leg gully. A leg bye taken.
STREAKY FOUR! Rabada serves a sharp length ball in the line of the stumps and Santner is opened up in defense. The outside edge which is generated speeds wide of the slip cordon for a boundary.
Excellent delivery. On a length around middle, angling away, Santner drops his wrists and sways away from the line.
Pitches it full and on off, Nicholls drives it through mid off for a single.
Bouncer around leg, Nicholls ducks and the keeper stretches to his right to make an outstanding stop.
FOUR! Gets off the mark, Santner! Short of a length ball on off, Santner is on the back foot in a flash and hammer-pulls it to the deep mid-wicket fence.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Whoa! Some serious turn there. Drifting into the batsman, landing on middle and spinning away big. Santner tries to drive but misses. It beats the keeper and first slip and goes towards third man. Three byes taken.
Flatter and shorter on off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Santner has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Piedt to continue. A slip, gully, silly point and short leg in place.
Full in length and angling across the batsman, it's an easy leave for Nicholls.
Wrong line, bowls it on a fuller length and down the leg side, Nicholls tries to flick but misses. Rabada has been off target in this innings.
Fullish and on off, Nicholls is on the front foot as he pushes it to short extra cover.
On a length and outside off, shaping away, Nicholls pokes at it and misses.
Straighter in line, turned in the gap at square leg for a couple of runs.
EDGY FOUR! Good length ball angling away from the batsman, Nicholls gets squared up in defense and the outside edge races through gully for a boundary.
A touch short and on off, Santner goes back and punches it straight to covers.
Gets forward and defends it quietly to the leg side.
Wide outside off, spinning further away, Santner allows it through to the keeper.
Flatter ball on middle, defended off the back foot to the leg side.
Spinning away from the batsman, left alone by Santner.
Flighted ball on off, Santner gets forward and defends it to point.
Movement away from the batsman, Nicholls pushes inside the line and misses.

Stifled appeal for a catch! Down the leg side, on a length, the batsman fails to flick and it goes off his pads to the keeper. de Kock collects the ball to his right and then joins Rabada in appealing. Nothing from the umpire.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Right in the blockhole, Nicholls digs it out at the last moment.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Sharp delivery, a touch short and down the leg side, Nicholls tries to flick but misses. Good take with one hand by de Kock.
Santner has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

STUMPING CHANCE MISSED! Big charge from Santner first ball but it the ball curls away to beat his bat. de Kock fails to collect it and Amla collects it at first slip. Definitely a stumping chance goes down.
MITCHELL SANTNER is the new batsman.

OUT! The decision stays and it's a big blow to New Zealand! Piedt serves a tossed up off spinner and lands it outside off, Watling shuffles across the stumps and tries to flick but misses. He is thudded on the pads, they appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Watling takes the referral and the replays show that it's hit him in line and clipping the top of leg stump.  End of a 68-run stand and South Africa are five wickets away from winning the series 1-0!
Watling is given out lbw and he has reviewed it.
Short and wide outside off, Nicholls rocks back and punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
Flatter off spinner on off, Watling gets across the stumps and works it through square leg for a single.
Big spin down the leg side, Watling fails to flick and it's a good take by de Kock. He appeals as well for a catch but nothing from the umpire.

Appeal for an lbw! Sharp delivery by Rabada, in the line of the stumps and on a back of a length, Nicholls fails to get it away and is hit high on the pads. They appeal but the umpire shakes his head.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under it at the last moment.

Fullish on middle, it's flicked on the leg side and Bavuma shows good reflexes at short leg to stop the ball on one bounce. He is very sharp in that zone, probably the best going around at the moment!
Goes full with his length and lands it around off, Nicholls lunges and defends it to the off side.
Back of a length ball on off, Nicholls jumps on the back foot and defends it on the leg side.
An over-pitched ball on off, Nicholls drives it down the ground for a couple of runs. There was no mid off in place.
Flighted ball on off, Watling is on the front foot as he defends it down safely.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Uppish but safe! Tossed up ball outside off, Henry plays an uppish sweep shot and Bavuma at short leg anticipates it to his left but it goes past his right hand side. A single taken.
Flighted on off, spinning away, Nicholls goes back and taps it down to point.
Play and a miss! Short and wide outside off, Henry tries to cut but misses due to the extra bounce.
Flatter ball around leg, Watling gets across the stumps and turns it through backward square leg for a single.
DANE PIEDT is into the attack now.
Length ball down the leg side, Nicholls tries to flick but misses.

And this one shoots up after landing. A good length ball outside off, Nicholls shoulders arms and de Kock stretches to his left to collect the ball. Variable bounce is always tough to handle and it becomes deadly if it's in the line of the stumps. Ross Taylor has already been undone by it!
That stayed low again! On a length and outside off, Nicholls stays back to hit it through the line but it beats the bottom part of the bat.
Good length delivery outside off, Nicholls shoulders arms.
Down the leg side, a pacey delivery, Nicholls is beaten for pace as he tries to work. It goes off his thigh pad to leg gully.
Length ball on middle, Nicholls stays back to cover the line and helps it on the leg side. Straight to short leg.
Some extra bounce there, around leg, BJ fails to work it around and is hit on the thigh pad.
Outside off on a fuller length, it's forced in the gap at covers for a single.
Full in length and in the line of the stumps, Nicholls gets forward and drives it down to mid on.
This one is very wide outside off and easily left by Henry.
Cchooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Length ball angling away from the left-hander, Nicholls gets forward and drives it to point.
Another bouncer and Watling finds it easy to let it go over his head.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to duck underneath it.

FOUR! That was uppish but safe! A length delivery in the zone outside off, Watling gets forward to drive it through the line but it comes off the outside half of the bat and flies over point for a boundary.
Good length delivery outside off, Watling leaves it and de Kock fumbles while collecting the ball. They take a couple of byes.
FOUR! Shot! A shortish ball on off, Watling gets on top of the bounce and smashes it square of the wicket on the off side for a boundary.
Wrong start, full and down the leg side, Watling tries to flick but misses.
KAGISO RABADA is back into the attack.
Fullish and on off, Henry gets forward, opens the face of the bat and keeps it out safely on the off side.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
On a length and outside off, curling away, Nicholls allows it through to the keeper.
FOUR! Top shot! Back of a length ball on off, Nicholls transfers his weight on the back foot and punches it sweetly through covers for a glorious boundary. 50-run stand comes up!
Wayward delivery, wide outside off, another leave from Nicholls.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
Gentle delivery landing on a length but it has some inward movement, Watling does well to play it late and dabs it down towards point.
Philander bowls a full ball and keeps his line closer to the off stump, Watling has to play at it and he does so by getting on the front foot. Defended towards covers.
Hurls across a full length ball outside off, holding its line, Watling watches the line closely before leaving it for the keeper.
Length ball on off, Watling covers the line and defends it watchfully.

Almost drags it on! Shortish ball on off, some extra bounce too, Watling decides to defend it from the crease but it catches the bottom edge and goes on one bounce over the stumps. Near clipped the bails. Philander cannot believe his luck.
Angles in a length ball on off, straightening a touch, Watling opens up in defense and taps it down in front of the fourth slip fielder.
Too wide on this occasion and Nicholls has another easy leave.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
In the channel outside off, Nicholls has nothing to do with it.
Length delivery in the channel outside off, Nicholls shoulders arms.
Lands it on a length and around off, Nicholls gets forward and defends it near his front pad.
What a delivery! Van Zyl bowls it on a length outside off, Nicholls leaves it alone and the ball shoots up from the pitch. de Kock has to jump to collect the ball.
STIAAN VAN ZYL comes into the attack. He is a part-timer who bowls handy seam-up deliveries...
A harmless delivery, wide outside off, another comfortable leave for the Kiwi wicketkeeper batsman.

This one hardly carries to the keeper! Philander lets out a full ball outside off, an outswinger, Watling covers the line and leaves it alone. de Kock struggles to stop it but does well to not allow any bye.
Some away movement on this occasion but it's too wide outside off to bother the batsman. An easy leave for BJ!
Serves a good length ball on off, Watling once again keeps it out on the off side, not in the gap.
Length ball on off, Watling presses forward and defends it to the off side.
A length ball on middle, Nicholls turns it in the gap at mid-wicket for a single.
Drinks are on the field!
Fuller ball on off, the batsman has got nothing to offer on that one.

FOUR BYES! Wayward line by Rabada, there! Slips this one down the leg side, Watling tries chasing it but fails to get any wood on that one. Poor de Kock dives full length to his right but couldn't stop it from crossing the fence.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Back of a length delivery on middle, defended off the back foot gently.
FOUR! Crackling shot from Watling! An overpitched delivery on off, Watling loves it. He leans into it and sends it off the carpet through covers for a boundary. It sped away to the fence.
Short of a length delivery, swings a bit too much. BJ looks to cut it through point but gets beaten. Shouldn't touch those which are served too wide.
Short of a length delivery outside off, punched off the back foot towards covers.
Fuller and curling back in, Nicholls gets on the front foot to defend but gets a slight inside edge on the pads.
Gets behind the line and defends it towards the man at covers.
Angles a length delivery on middle and leg, Nicholls is beaten by the sharp swing there. Is hit on the box.
Wide! Full length delivery outside off, actually very wide outside off. No trouble for Nicholls.

Full and slipping down the leg side, Henry looks to flick it through the on side but misses as the ball brushes his pads and goes back. de Kock dives to his right and denies it from running down to the boundary.
A harmless delivery in the vicinity outside off, Nicholls ignores.
VERNON PHILANDER is back into the attack!
Good length ball and once again it is on the pads, HN clips it past Bavuma at short leg to keep strike.
Fuller on middle and leg, worked towards mid-wicket.
Fuller and angled on the pads, clipped just past short leg.
Covers the line and answers it with a straight bat.

NOT OUT! South Africa waste a review here! Rabada bangs it short on middle, Nicholls gets back to flick it on the leg side but misses it. The ball lobs of something towards short leg and Bavuma standing there takes it. They all go up in an appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Henry immediately opts for the review and the replays show it was a right call from the batsman. The ball lobbed off the thigh pad.
Nicholls is given out caught at short leg by the on-field umpire. But he wants to review it.
Short of a length delivery down the leg side, Nicholls looks to pull but fails to do so.
Another maiden! Fuller length and angling in, worked towards mid on.

Just short of Bavuma! Short of a length delivery on middle, Watling gets back and looks to tuck it on the leg side. The bounce gets big on him and he ends up playing it in front of Bavuma at short leg who collects it on one bounce.
On a length and outside off, Watling pushes it towards the man at point.
Short of a length delivery on middle, Watling crouches to let that one sail over him to the keeper.
Pitches it up this time and around off, BJ leans ahead and pushes it towards the man at covers.

Lovely ball! Short of a length delivery, close to the off stump line. Some gentle bounce that Steyn gets and puts every batsman in trouble. Watling looks to play it inside the line only to get beaten up.
Back of a length ball on middle, defended from within the crease.
Shorter ball on off, punched off the back foot for a single.
Short ball outside off, Watling stands up and looks to defend it but the ball beats his outside edge.
FOUR! Beautifully played! Watling is recovering well after getting hit on the shoulders. Full outside off, he steps forward and drives it gracefully through the covers for a sweeping boundary.
Fullish ball on the pads, Nicholls works it to square leg for a single.
Wide! Angles across, that full delivery was miles away from the batsman. He leaves it and the umpire signals a wide.
Length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.
KAGISO RABADA comes into the attack.
Outside off and Watling misses that one too.
Good length ball around off, Watling looks to defend and his bat's outside edge is beaten.

OUCH! That is going to hurt! Length ball on the stumps, Watling misjudges the bounce and is quick to duck under it. Instead the ball comes on straight and smacks into his shoulder. Watling is sure to feel that tomorrow morning.
Fuller ball around off, pushed to the covers.
On the stumps, Watling plays it to point.
BEATEN! Length ball outside off and seaming away, Watling looks to defend it to the off side but is beaten.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Fuller length ball on the stumps, Watling works it to mid-wicket. He finds the gap and the ball crosses the ropes.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Back of a length ball outside off, punched off the back foot.
Good length ball outside off, defended off the front foot with a straight bat.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Bouncer! Nicholls sways back to avoid it.
Down the leg side and zipping in again, Nicholls looks to work it but is hit on the thigh pad.
Bouncer! Henry ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Nasty! That short delivery was deadly accurate and hits Watling on the glove as he looks to defend. The batsmen pick up a single.
Short delivery on middle and off, worked down the leg side for a single.
In the corridor outside off, left alone.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads.
Length ball around off, Watling looks to play it but misses.
On the stumps, defended off the back foot.

NOT OUT! Decision stays! Down the leg side with extra bounce again and Watling goes after it. He misses and the ball goes to the keeper who pouches the sitter. There appears to be a slight deflection and the fielding side appeal loudly. The umpire isn't impressed but the fielding side thinks otherwise. They discuss amongst themselves and go for a review. The replays show that there was an edge but it is yet to be answered whether it was the arm or glove. UltraEdge confirms the edge with a small blip and things look to be going in SA's favour. However, in a shift of fortunes, the third umpire decides in favour of NZ. Slightly confusing decision but Watling is happy to go with it.
South Africa has decided to review a catch appeal of BJ Watling.
Shorter ball on off, defended from within the crease.
Seaming in on leg, Watling looks to flick it but misses and is struck on the pads.
Full ball on middle and leg, flicked to square leg for a single.
Shorter ball outside off, Watling places his bat in the line of the delivery to block it but the ball swings away again.
Bouncer! Watling does well to evade it.
Back of a length ball outside off, defended from within the crease.
Fuller on the stumps, defended off the front foot with a straight bat.
Length ball and swinging away, Watling lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Short ball on middle and leg, played off the front foot and into the ground.

DROPPED! How could he miss that one?! Good length delivery outside off, Watling looks to push it to the off side but edges it to the slips. The ball carries, going to the fielder at second slip but an over eager van Zyl at third slip dives across and fluffs it. The ball rides up his forearms and passes through for a single. Watling has just dodged a bullet and Vernon Philander is not a happy man.
The ball is too wide on the off side for Watling to make any contact.
Length ball outside off, Watling leaves it.
Length ball outside off, Nicholls miscues it to the slips. A couple of shouts but the ball doesn't carry.
A swing and a miss! Short and outside off, Nicholls looks to cut it but misjudges the bounce and the ball beats the bat's bottom edge.
Length ball outside off, Watling plays it to point.
In the corridor outside off, Watling leaves it.
Another one angled away outside off, Watling looks to defend it but the ball swings away and he misses.
Angled away and outside off, Watling shoulders his arms.
Well outside off, Watling hesitates a bit and leaves it.
Back of a length ball around off, defended off the back foot.
DALE STEYN to bowl from the other end.
FOUR! CLASSICAL! Nicholls is showing some artful batting skills. Full outside off, he strides forward and drives it smoothly through mid off and the ball races to the boundary line.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Wide outside off stump, Henry leaves it alone.
Length ball outside off, Nicholls looks to defend it but the ball seams in and hits his thigh pad.

FOUR! BEAUTIFULLY PLAYED! Nicholls starts the session off on the right foot. The ball drifts into the legs and Nicholls goes back and clips it neatly through square leg and across the ropes. They still need a a massive 378 though.
Shorter ball down the leg side, worked to the leg side.
We are back for the afternoon session. The players are out in the middle and it will be HENRY NICHOLLS and BJ WATLING whi will continue to bat. VERNON PHILANDER is back on with the ball.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...
"For those who were thinking Dale Steyn was done. Here is the gentle reminder.beware the emotionally injured animal", tweets the former South African cricketer HD Ackerman.

Latham and Guptill were scalped by Steyn in the very first over, but the 'Steyn Gun' wasn't done though, sending Taylor packing on a duck. Vernon Philander waltzed in and picked up the prized wicket of skipper Williamson, who wasn't looking at his best with a finger injury. Faf du Plessis will be a happy man as New Zealand shift focus to battling for survival and pride. Join us at 1610 IST as we follow the Kiwi struggle.

In the first half on the session, Temba Bavuma fulfilled his role for the hosts, gently piling up the runs and playing it safe. The Proteas then decided to declare early, putting a 400-run target squarely on the shoulders of The Black Caps. New Zealand came on but were unprepared for the blitz that hit them.

Spectacular doesn't even begin to describe the fireworks we have witnessed in the latter half of the morning session. New Zealand are in deep, deep trouble here and it is all due to the firebrand that is Dale Steyn. He didn't wait a moment in launching into an attack that is almost solely responsible for bringing the visitors' batting line up to their knees.
Yes he does! A length ball outside off, at 139.9 kph, BJ Watling lifts his bat and lets it go through to de Kock. THAT'S LUNCH ON DAY 4!
That's the length that is troubling the Kiwis. Steyn dishes a length ball on off, curls away a bit. Watling nearly gets an outside edge. Can he survive on the last ball before lunch?
Back of a length ball on off, Watling gets back and pushes it towards point.

FOUR! Steyn is hit for a boundary, would you believe it? He keeps it full outside off, Watling leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary. No need to run for those. That should give Watling some sort of confidence.
In the channel on off, Watling shoulders his arms to that one.
Fuller length ball on off, keeps shaping away from the batsman. Watling lets it go through to the keeper.
FOUR! Edged away! Bowls it on a length and outside off, Nicholls gets an outside edge which flies past 4th slip for a boundary towards third man.
Outside off, it's left alone.
Leg bye! Length ball on the pads, Watling looks to flick but it goes off his pads towards the on side. They cross for a leg bye.
Pushed towards covers for a single.
"Every time Dale Steyn's career record comes on screen I suddenly remember I'm watching a historical great of the game. Unbelievable." tweets the Kiwi all-rounder Jimmy Neesham.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Watling punches it towards the man at covers.
Switches his angle and comes from over the wicket now, bowls another short ball. Nicholls crouches down to evade it.
Angles a length delivery on middle, Nicholls presses forward and defends it down.
Short of a length delivery on middle, Nicholls offers a straight bat.
Bangs it short from round the wicket, Henry ducks under it with sanity.
The batsman appears to have been struck on the thigh-pad.
Full and angling on middle, Nicholls looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.
Landed outside off, pushed towards point.
Full and outside off, Watling lets it go through to the keeper.
On a good length and outside off, BJ covers the line and defends it down.
Fuller length delivery on off, Watling lifts his bat and allows it to go through to the keeper.
On a length and outside off, Watling defends it off the back foot comfortably.
BJ WATLING is the new man in.

OUT! Edged and what a brilliant take by Quinton de Kock! Mind boggling stuff from the Proteas. Though the wicket will go down in Philander's kitty but this is de Kock's wicket, mind you. Hurls a length delivery outside off, swings away after pitching. Williamson gets back to punch it through covers but much to his dismay he ends up getting an outside edge towards the keeper. QDK dives full length to his right and pulls off a screamer. He almost dived in front of Amla at first slip, terrific work. This is disappointing for the Kiwis as the skipper falls cheaply too.

Edged but safe! Steyn is seriously troubling the Kiwis here. Mind you, Rabada is still not introduced into the attack. Anyway, this one was a short ball, served in the channel on off, Nicholls looks to defend but gets an outside edge through vacant backward point for a couple.
HENRY NICHOLLS is the next batsman in.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! The 'Steyn Gun' bags another one and also equals Ntini's record who holds the highest no. of wickets at this venue - 54. This was another full length delivery on middle, moves away nicely but it doesn't rise much off the deck. Taylor can't be blamed here as he didn't expect it at all. The ball hits him on the back pad and right in front of the stumps. Steyn goes up in an appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Taylor walks to Williamson and has a chat but decides not to take a review. Three down are the Kiwis and are in dire straits here.
Fuller length ball on off, Taylor leaves it alone this time.
This is brilliant bowling from Dale! He once again pitches it up on off, shapes away a touch. Taylor looks to poke at it but the ball whizzes past the outside edge to de Kock.
Fuller length delivery in the channel on off, asking Taylor to go for it. He almost made his mind and is lucky not to edge this one to the keeper.
Fuller length delivery on middle, swings away a bit. Taylor lunges forward and defends it solidly.
Williamson is now getting some hot water treatment... An ideal option is to walk off if that is hurting badly.
Back of a length ball on off, defended watchfully off the back foot.
Fuller and slants it down the leg side, Williamson looks to flick it down the leg side but misses.
Angles a length delivery around middle and leg, Williamson gets across and tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Kane gets back and taps it in front of gully.

The physio is out as Williamson is getting his finger taped. He is taking a painkiller, a bandage is applied too. He is not looking comfortable out there, these are worrying signs for the Kiwis. Their go-to man is looking in some serious pain out there but he is a brave lad, wants to battle.
On a length and outside off, Williamson gets behind the line and defends it towards covers.
Vernon Philander shares the new cherry from the other end. Fuller and angled on middle, Williamson gets across and flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.

OUT! Steyn strikes again in the very first over. A wicket on the first and last ball and both the Kiwi openers are back in the hut, bagging a golden duck each. This is some start, the Steyn that we all know and love. New Zealand in all sorts of trouble here. Coming to the ball, he bowls on a length and gets it to shape away from the batsman, Guptill pokes at it and pays the price for the same. The extra bounce is there once again and hence Martin gets a thick outside edge that flies in the safe hands of Amla at first slip. He doesn't drop many and this one is no different. South Africa are off to a flier here. Ross Taylor in next with New Zealand in early trouble.
Good length delivery on off, Williamson punches it towards covers for a single.
On a length and around off, Williamson looks to play it with soft hands and is lucky to get an outside edge which falls short of the man at second slip.
Strays it down the leg side, Kane has got nothing to with that one.
Williamson off the mark! On a length and moves away this time. Williamson opens the face of the bat and guides it past gully for a couple.
The skipper and the reliable man, KANE WILLIAMSON is the new man in.

OUT! Bam goes the timberrrrrr! Dale Steyn provides his team just the start they wanted. He starts with a short of length delivery on off. Tom Latham as every batsman would do, tries to shoulder his arms but there is some extra bounce as the ball catches the gloves and then crashes on to the woodwork. Steyn is all pumped up and sprints towards the slip cordon to get a pat on the back. New Zealand rocked early here.
